posts.name: jffdougan
posts.cooked:
Given the part of the Daredevil run they look to be drawing from, Fisk seems likely to be the villain again.

As for probable timings: We get aka Jessica Jones and Luke Cage next, I think in that order. Per IMDB listings, akaJJ is a December premiere, Luke Cage will be sometime next year. Netflix is pretty good about putting their new seasons for shows in the same month as the original, so Daredevil S2 will probably be late March 2016 (IMDB currently says April). Iron Fist will be at the end of the cycle for the original four, so almost certainly after Daredevil S2 (which will give them some time to elaborate on Madame Gao's "much farther away than China" comment).

Only after Iron Fist has had his own installment can we get the Defenders mini-series.

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked:
That was a lot of fun!

I have read Daredevil, not all, probably not a lot, but enough and the series I just watched felt a lot like the more recent comics, and that was goooooood.

I actually liked the characters, I can't think of a single one that felt like a waste or was acted badly, not even the bit parts.

There were character deaths that actually mattered, huzzah for that (even if I didn't want them to die) and (until the end) scenes showing Fisk as not just a stereotypical bad guy from the comics, and very little over-the-top comic book influence.

So many nods to what has come before though, not invasive but prominent enough to be noticed by those looking.

 

Throughout the whole of the series there were only two bum notes for me, the cliffhanger ending to the 1st of the of 2-part Russian brothers' episode (why the hell do you need a cliff hanger in a show that has no schedule or advertising?) and the final fight with Fisk. All the other fights had impact when fist met body, this just sounded like wet noodles in comparison.

 

For next season the only thing I want is more interaction between Foggy and Daredevil (as opposed to Matt), I want to see a more open relationship between them, not having to sneak around behind Karen's back, that usually reduces itself to farce far to quickly.

 

EDIT: Actually, next season I'd like NO Fisk, move on to a completely different thing, and then third season do an adaptation of Brubaker's Daredevil in prison arc, with Fisk inside at the sametime, I think that would be a lot of fun.

 

 

Phew!

That was a difficult day-and-a-bit watching all those episodes so I could participate in the discussion here, at least I don't have to do that again!

*Sees S.H.I.E.L.D. thread*

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
Fisk was a reeeaaaaaally interesting villain in this show. (Vincent D’Onofio helped. “PUT MY…HANDS…ON MY HEAD…LIKE THIS?”) What the show did really well was portraying him as sympathetic, awkward first dates and all, without ever losing the sense that he was the villain. They humanized him without ever relying on some “oh, he’s just misunderstood” cliche.

(Tangent: I wonder if they used Whitey Bulger for inspiration?)

I think the end set up for Fisk to break out of prison. He kind of went through a Doctor Horrible-ish arc, where he had this cognitive dissonance that he was trying to make the city better…but by the end, he’s 100% bad guy. And the bad guy always breaks out of prison for next week’s episode.
